measurement_head.reading: Measured from the sensor axis the four edge tests are exactly what the organizers intended at every range (#4 on the edge, #6 inside, #5 and #7 outside: 74 / 93 frames inside, 0 / 0). Measured from the rails they are not (#4 16, #6 8 frames inside; #5 98, #7 58). What each variant can change: #5 and #7 lie on the side where the axis envelope is NARROWER than the rail envelope, so a union adds nothing there by construction; #4 and #6 lie on the widened side. Two rules besides the envelope decide #4 and #6: #4 is demoted as floating whatever the reference (outermost point 1.04-1.23 m from the axis > 0.95 m), and #6's in-corridor strip is dropped as a wall whenever its mean lateral exceeds 1.2 m (from the axis it is ~1.18-1.19 m, borderline). A union of the membership alone therefore cannot win #4, and wins #6 only where its cluster survives and confirms (5 hits).

preregistered.before_any_result: No candidate code exists and no candidate has been run. Known before this file: the HEAD measurement above (scratch script, set O only).
preregistered.region: Both candidates act only where the two references agree: the frame has the rail pair in the near range (track.rail_slabs > 0) and |track.curvature| <= gauge.axis_union_max_curvature = 2e-4 /m (R >= 5 km, straight track: the rails' estimate on set O is <= 6.2e-5); per point, range_min <= X <= gauge.axis_union_range = 50 m (near field) and |c(X)| <= gauge.axis_union_max_offset = 0.30 m, where c(X) = track.center_y(X) is the rail axis in the processed frame, whose X axis is the sensor axis when the mount calibration applies no yaw (always below calibration.min_yaw_deg = 3 deg). 0.30 m is below the 0.35 m advisory margin, so the union never reaches beyond the rail advisory corridor. On a curve the sensor axis leaves the track as X^2 / 2R (0.6 m at 50 m on R 2 km): the curvature bound excludes curves, the offset bound whatever is left.
preregistered.flags: gauge.axis_union (0 = off, the default and byte-identical output; 1 = candidate A; 2 = candidate B), gauge.axis_union_range 50.0, gauge.axis_union_max_offset 0.30, gauge.axis_union_max_curvature 2e-4

A.rule: strict-envelope membership of a corridor candidate = membership measured from the rails (edge margin included, as now) OR, inside the region, membership of (y_axis = dy + c(X), h) in the same polygon with the same edge margin. Nothing else changes: the candidates (the rail advisory corridor already contains the region's axis envelope), every lateral, signature and distance stay measured from the rails.

B.rule: inside the region the corridor coordinate itself is re-measured on the side towards which the sensor axis lies off the rail axis (s = -sign c(X), e = |c(X)|, u = s * dy >= 0): u' = max(u - e, u * W / (W + e)), W = the envelope half-width 1.05 m; the other side and everything outside the region unchanged. Continuous and monotone; strict membership is then exactly the union (edge margin applied to u'); beyond W + e the lateral is the one from the sensor axis (u - e), so the advisory corridor also extends by e on that side, and the cluster lateral, the infrastructure and signature rules (wall 1.2 m, floating 0.95 m, ...), the hanging stage and the clear-distance cap read the re-measured coordinate. The bed template, the low-object stage and the ego-speed texture keep the rail coordinate.

preregistered.excluded: The axis-only envelope (replace the rails by the sensor axis in the near field) is not a candidate: on the side where the axis envelope is narrower it gives up up to 0.3 m of the rail envelope, i.e. the space the train actually sweeps (it follows the rails), so it can lose a real object by construction; its per-frame decisions are the 'from the axis' counts above. A change of floating_free_max_dy (the only way to win #4) is a different rule and is not tried here.
preregistered.ship_rule: A candidate ships only if (1) on set O #4 and #6 together gain STOP frames and neither loses any; (2) NO new STOP frame on #5, #7 or the background (background alarm frames and track ids not higher); (3) the full gate (python scripts/regression_gate.py --cache /data/cache --jobs 1 --baseline docs/evidence/results/regression_baseline_2026-09-25_ride_p3b.json) exits 0 with no gated row worse; (4) every safety condition holds. If both pass, the one with more #4 + #6 STOP frames ships; a tie ships A (the smaller change).
